title: Review of c04's crawler confound finding: replicates on fresh seed 3 (clipped term: founder dead by t~50; bV=1 starved at t=300: 14 bodies persist as static ghosts to t=600)
summary: Ran the finding's world.py on seed 3 three ways (T=600): unchanged (15 bodies, 12 persistent splits, gen 5, top track 14.9 BL), okclip=1 in full food (the planted founder is gone between t=25 and t=50, nothing ever reforms), and bV=1 with all food removed at t=300 (14 bodies at t=300 stay 14 to t=600). In the starved run's sheet the crawlers lose their content and polarization within ~60 t and become round, static, uniform diffuse spots that never dissolve. Both halves of the finding replicate: without the negative branch the founder cannot pay for crawling, and with it starved bodies do not die.

observations.E: counts_s3.txt: okclip founder 1 -> 0 by frame 20 (t=50); bV starve 14 bodies at frame 120 (t=300) and 14 at frame 240 (t=600); rerun/bV_starve/seed3/sheet.png t=362-600: static round ghosts with no content

seeds_run.result: bV starve: no deaths after food removal
base world divides (12 persistent splits, gen 5)

controls_run.E: rerun/base/seed3 (unclipped, fed) against rerun/okclip/seed3 and rerun/bV_starve/seed3, same seed

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed. I did not probe delta inside the ghosts (the author's ghost_probe); the persistence is seen in counts and images. The founder is planted, so this world is not S whatever the term does.
